title: Shared ingest counters across telemetry worker threads
name: Telemetry ingest worker pool

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how the worker threads update the shared counters? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does flush() use Atomics.exchange for accepted/rejected/bytes rather than a load followed by a store of 0?
choices: exchange is required to read BigInt64Array values
A separate load and store would let increments made by workers between the two operations be lost; exchange reads and resets in one atomic step
exchange wakes workers blocked on the counter
exchange makes the reported values monotonic across flushes

questions.prompt: Why is the inflight slot read with snapshot() instead of being drained like the other counters?
choices: inflight is a gauge of current work that begin()/end() raise and lower; resetting it to 0 would make later end() calls drive it negative
inflight is only written by the main thread, so it needs no atomic reset
drainCounters cannot reset more than three slots

questions.prompt: A frame fails to decode in a worker. Which counters change, once the handler returns?
choices: rejected +1 and inflight unchanged, but bytes also increases
Only inflight +1, because return skips the finally block
rejected +1, and inflight returns to its prior value
